hypotheses.reasoning: redis-cache was restarted after a node replacement at 07:40:07 with no RDB snapshot, so it came back with 0 keys (#2228). Before that the cache was healthy, with a low miss rate. Afterwards search-api's miss ratio jumped to 96% against a 3% baseline, and every miss went to catalog-db (#2372). That cache stampede pushed catalog-db to 485/500 connections and 96% CPU (#2317), and simple point lookups slowed to 3-8s (#2414, #2638). search-api's product queries then timed out after 5000ms (#2410, #2733), which caused the web-bff GET /search 504s and high p99. catalog-db was healthy before 07:40 (only vacuum and checkpoint lines). The small trigger, a cold cache, was amplified by the load from cache misses.

verdict.recommendedAction: Shed or rate-limit the cache-miss load on catalog-db: add request coalescing (single-flight) or a lock around cache fills in search-api, and pre-warm redis-cache with hot product keys. Add capacity or limit concurrency on catalog-db until the cache hit rate is back to normal. Going forward, enable RDB/AOF persistence or warm the cache before node replacement. Separately, move notif-worker's poison message msg-759587 (offset 829709) to a dead-letter queue.
